1x91nj6: Just one question: who does the second action?
ijar33: Many verbs you already know (_querer, preferir, necesitar, esperar, desear_), emotions (_me alegra, me molesta, me da miedo_) and judgements (_es importante, es mejor_) follow the same rule. If the second action is done by **the same person**, use the **infinitive**. If it is done by **another person**, use **que + subjunctive**.
1kssfk8: _Prefiero subir temprano_ (I prefer, I go up). _Prefiero que subas temprano_ (I prefer, you go up). _Me alegra estar aquí_ (I'm glad, I'm here). _Me alegra que estés aquí_ (I'm glad, you're here).
1aiksbj: With judgements, the infinitive is a general rule and _que_ + subjunctive points to someone specific: _Es importante beber agua en la altura_ / _Es importante que Hannah beba agua_.
fy02tt: The same person wants and gets to know: **infinitive**.
pyshg7: With a different subject you need **que**: _espero que llegues_.
qmcaq0: Permitir, prohibir, dejar: two correct forms
124z3wf: With **permitir, prohibir, dejar, aconsejar, recomendar** and **obligar a**, the person who receives the permission or prohibition appears in the pronoun (_me, te, le, nos, les_). That is why you can use the infinitive even though there are two people: _Rocío le prohíbe salir_ = _Rocío le prohíbe que salga_.
lhh1jd: Don't put **de** before the infinitive: _te prohíbo salir_, not _te prohíbo de salir_. With **obligar** you do need **a**: _El guía nos obliga a llevar casco_.

poun8t: The imperative: only one form of its own
11i16zv: Only the **affirmative tú** order (and the vosotros one) has its own form: _espera, sube, ven, di, haz, pon, sal, ten, ve, sé_. **All the others** are the present subjunctive you already reviewed in week 2: negative tú (_no subas_), usted (_suba, no suba_), ustedes (_suban, no suban_) and nosotros (_subamos_).
14iqge2: Pronouns go **after and attached** in affirmative orders (_siéntese, dímelo, tráiganlas_) and **before** in negative ones (_no se siente, no me lo digas, no las traigan_). When you attach pronouns, many forms need a written accent to keep their stress: _di_ → _dímelo_.

2wgxw: Passing on an order: dile que venga
5wkinz: When an order **passes through another person**, the imperative becomes **que + subjunctive**: _«Ven a las siete»_ → _Dile que venga a las siete_; _Patricio dice que vengas a las siete_; _Te pide que vengas a las siete_.
1ykzlx4: When you pass on the order, **the person of the verb** and **the pronouns** change: Patricio says to Hannah _«Mándame el documento»_ and Rocío passes it on like this: _Dice que se lo mandes_.
oz9bkp: In conversation, **que** at the beginning is enough: _Que pase_ (an order for someone who isn't talking to you), _—¿Qué dice? —Que subas_ (repeating an order).
